original_question: Which combinatorial symmetry type graphs occur among convex polytopes, and which geometric symmetry type graphs occur among convex polytopes?
target_in_paper: The open problem in the paper’s symmetry-type-graph cluster asking for a realizability/classification of symmetry type graphs for convex polytopes, separated into the combinatorial and geometric settings.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the key invariant from the paper—symmetry type graphs—and it also correctly preserves the paper’s essential split between combinatorial and geometric realizability. It is also appropriately scoped to convex polytopes rather than to all abstract polytopes or maniplexes.
missing_details: It should explicitly say that the question is about realizability/classification: given a candidate symmetry type graph, determine whether there exists a convex polytope realizing it.
It should define a symmetry type graph as the quotient of the flag graph by flag-orbits under the relevant group action.
It should distinguish the two relevant group actions: combinatorial automorphisms of the polytope versus geometric symmetries of a convex realization.
It should make clear that the two questions are separate: one for combinatorial symmetry type graphs and one for geometric symmetry type graphs.
It should specify that the ambient objects are finite convex polytopes in Euclidean space, not arbitrary abstract polytopes/maniplexes unless stated otherwise.
It should avoid the vague phrase 'occur among convex polytopes' and replace it with 'occur as the combinatorial/geometric symmetry type graph of some convex polytope'.
No ring/field, operator, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic-quantifier data are relevant here; the missing information is definitional and scope-related rather than algebraic.
refined_question: Which symmetry type graphs are realizable by convex polytopes? More precisely: classify those edge-coloured quotient graphs that arise as (i) the combinatorial symmetry type graph of a convex polytope, meaning the quotient of its flag graph by its combinatorial automorphism group, and separately (ii) the geometric symmetry type graph of a convex polytope, meaning the quotient of its flag graph by the geometric symmetry group of a convex realization.
justification: The paper is explicitly a survey of open problems on k-orbit polytopes, and your draft clearly points to the symmetry-type-graph portion rather than to the rooted-polytope preliminaries. The closest paper-faithful sharpening is therefore a realizability/classification question about symmetry type graphs for convex polytopes, with the paper’s own combinatorial-versus-geometric distinction made explicit. I did not broaden the question to abstract polytopes or maniplexes in general, because your draft is already anchored to convex polytopes. I also did not replace 'symmetry type graph' by a looser 'k-orbit type' formulation, since the graph itself is the paper’s sharper invariant. Exact in-paper numbering/page location could not be recovered from the abstract page alone, but the target problem is unambiguous from the paper’s scope and from later literature that cites the realizability of symmetry type graphs as a central open direction.
